On the rows the refusal printed: cash 7.31 basis -0.65 needs 796c, the column reads 7.9625 which is -788.038c as cents and +0.25c as dollars; cash 7.15 basis -0.9 needs 805c, the column reads 8.0525 which is -796.947c as cents and +0.25c as dollars. Declared, not inferred, and self-checking: a wrong declaration is out by a hundredfold and the identity guard refuses it straight back.

CASH ROUNDING, MEASURED 2026-09-16 across 47 rows on the 25 cashbidssingle boards refused for this same reason: under the dollars hypothesis the residuals are -0.25c (17), +0c (2), +0.25c (24), +0.5c (4) and nothing else. Worst is 0.5c, they run in BOTH directions, and they sit on the quarter-cent grid — the board posts cash and basis to two decimals and its quote on the quarter cent, so the derived value is a whole number of cents and the quote is not. floor-cent does not describe this: it explains only the non-negative ones. round-cent-both bounds it at strictly under a cent either way, which is exactly what two cent-rounded columns can produce between them, and it still refuses every column shift, which moves things by tens of cents.
